name: Blinatumomab (CD19/CD3 BiTE) for relapsed/refractory or MRD-positive B-ALL

biomarkers.note: BIOMARKER GATE: blinatumomab is a CD19/CD3 bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE) and requires CD19-positive B-lineage ALL. DeVita 12th ed. line 32198 describes blinatumomab as a bispecific T-cell engager consisting of anti-CD3/anti-CD19; line 31889 names the anti-CD3/anti-CD19 molecule blinatumomab. Initial approval was in Philadelphia-negative relapsed/refractory B-ALL (DeVita lines 276510 to 276520); also used for MRD-positive disease.

lineOfTherapy: relapsed/refractory (salvage) or MRD-directed; frequently used to bridge to allogeneic stem-cell transplant

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: relapsed or refractory B-ALL, or MRD-positive B-ALL

drugs.name: Blinatumomab
drugs.notes: Blinatumomab is given as a continuous IV infusion over each treatment cycle (DeVita line 32198 describes the BiTE mechanism; the route is grounded, the dose is not). No adult mg/mcg-per-day dose or cycle schedule is printed in the adult ALL extracts - dose, unit, basis, and days are VERIFY (not inferred). The pediatric NCCN guideline (guidelines/ped_all.txt line 5328) prints a pediatric BSA-based step of 5 micrograms/m2/day for the first 7 days then 15 micrograms/m2/day; this is reference-only and is NOT adopted as the adult dose, which is weight-tiered fixed dosing per current label. A step-up (lead-in) dose to mitigate cytokine release syndrome is standard - confirm against the current label.

premedications.name: Corticosteroid pre-phase / premedication
premedications.notes: cytoreduction and dexamethasone premedication before and at infusion start/step-up are used to reduce cytokine release syndrome risk - confirm dose against the current label

supportiveCare: cytokine release syndrome (CRS) monitoring and management - a recognized class toxicity of T-cell-engaging therapy (DeVita lines 276613 to 276639 discuss CRS grading for immune effector cell therapies); confirm blinatumomab-specific mitigation (step-up dosing, corticosteroid, tocilizumab availability) against the current label
neurologic toxicity monitoring (encephalopathy, seizures, tremor, aphasia) - a recognized blinatumomab class toxicity; institute the label neurologic-event management and holding rules
tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis (hydration, allopurinol or rasburicase) especially with high tumor burden
CNS prophylaxis / intrathecal therapy remains required because antibodies do not enter the CNS (Harrison line 120148)
inpatient monitoring for cycle 1 / step-up per label; infusion-pump continuity is essential (continuous infusion)

monitoring: CRS surveillance (fever, hypotension, hypoxia) - especially during cycle 1 and each step-up
neurologic assessment at baseline and during infusion
tumor lysis labs early in cycle 1

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 or higher CRS or neurologic event
doseModificationRules.text: Interrupt/hold infusion and manage per label; physician decides on resumption and step-up.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 31889 (anti-CD3/anti-CD19 blinatumomab), 32198 (BiTE mechanism), 32272 to 32276 (randomized trial versus chemotherapy), 276510 to 276520 (Ph-negative relapsed/refractory B-ALL activity and 2016 approval), 276613 to 276639 (CRS and neurotoxicity grading for immune effector cell therapies)
line 120148 (intrathecal CNS prophylaxis required with immunotherapies because most antibodies do not enter the CNS)

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric ALL extract (reference only; pediatric dosing not adopted for adults)
guideline.locator: guidelines/ped_all.txt line 5328 (pediatric blinatumomab 5 then 15 micrograms/m2/day - reference only)

provenanceNote: Textbook-grounded StewardMD draft for relapsed/refractory or MRD-positive CD19-positive B-ALL. The CD19/CD3 BiTE identity, the CD19-positive biomarker gate, the continuous IV infusion route, the relapsed/refractory and MRD-positive setting, and the CRS/neurotoxicity safety profile are grounded in DeVita 12th ed. (lines 32198, 276510 to 276520, 276613 to 276639) with the intrathecal-CNS-prophylaxis requirement from Harrison line 120148. The adult per-day dose, step-up schedule, and cycle length are NOT printed in the adult extracts and are left VERIFY; the pediatric microgram/m2/day values are recorded as reference-only and are not adopted as the adult dose. NCCN per-disease template, StewardMD clinical (R1) review, and any hospital-implementation overlay approval are pending. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
